review_basis: Hand-traced in the running canvas app's Linear tool (manual mode, scale confirmed from the plan's own detected '3/16" = 1'-0"' note) via a Playwright-driven browser session against the rendered PDF. Before tracing, the run's own size label ('1 1/4"ø') and the coil callout it feeds ('HC 3' / 'CV 3') were confirmed against pdf.ts's positionedText output, and independently again against the raw vector geometry: the traced line's y-coordinate (page-space y=1302.7 of 3456, at the render's 2x-of-PDF-points viewport scale) matches, to sub-pixel precision, the endpoint of an explicit leader stroke dropping from the '1 1/4"ø' label's own drawn text box -- not just a nearby label inferred by proximity, but a leader line traced stroke-for-stroke from label to pipe. REVISED once (same day): the first pass traced only a 2.2 LF sub-span of this pipe -- the portion nearest the coil, chosen to keep the label-verification crop small -- which turned out to be an ARBITRARY interior point, not a real drawn stop (no fitting, no branch, no family change there). A dumb ruler doesn't know to stop at a point a human picked for narrative convenience; scoring trace_run's own honest full walk of the same straight run against that arbitrary sub-span produced a meaningless 257% 'over-trace' that was really just a golden that stopped short of where the geometry itself stops. Re-traced end to end: from the real riser-side gap (a dead end in the drawn linework, confirmed live via the canvas app's own snap + real-world coordinate readout) to the real crossing point the pipe passes through before its final elbow into the valve cluster -- both genuine geometric features, not narrative choices. `mcp/scripts/linear-trace-eval.mjs` independently re-confirmed the corrected extent: trace_run's own walk from a seed placed on this run reaches from x=2478.7 (dead_end) through x=2282.2 to an elbow, matching this golden's own re-traced endpoints px-for-px.
scope: This ITD Lab sheet (M1.2) is a dense hydronic distribution plan: a full HWS/HWR riser network feeding many HC/CV coil units, plus an unrelated STEAM branch serving a rooftop AHU. WP3.8 asks for a representative run here, not an exhaustive trace of the sheet. This golden is ONE branch run: the 1¼" pipe tapping off the building's HWS/HWR riser (at the point the riser breaks for its isolation-valve/circulator-pump cluster) and running to the elbow immediately ahead of coil unit HC-3/CV-3's own valve cluster -- a genuine dead-end-to-elbow geometric span, not an arbitrary interior sub-span (see review_basis for why that distinction matters for automated over-trace scoring). Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE, and deliberately left unresolved: (1) every other HC/CV coil branch on this sheet, the full riser run, and the STEAM system, left for a later, broader pass; (2) this sheet draws its HWS and HWR risers as a SINGLE overlapping vertical line with two stacked '1 1/2"ø' size labels rather than two visually separated lines, and the branch-off likewise splits into two closely-spaced (14px, ~0.5ft apart in page space) parallel 1¼" lines feeding separate isolation-valve/pump legs. This golden traces only ONE of those two lines (the upper of the pair). Which one is HWS and which is HWR could not be confirmed from the drawn geometry alone -- doing so would require reading the coil's own connection schedule or flow-direction convention beyond what this plan sheet shows -- so the run's system is recorded as the generic fluid code 'HHW' rather than guessing 'HWS' or 'HWR'. Withholding the supply/return distinction is deliberate, not an oversight: a wrong guess here would silently corrupt any score built on this golden. (3) linear-trace-eval.mjs's own run against this golden shows trace_run reading this run's size as a ROUND DUCT diameter ('round:1.25') rather than a pipe nominal size ('pipe:1.25') -- both notations share the same 'ø' glyph, and sizes.ts's grammar does not yet disambiguate them by sheet content (an all-piping sheet vs. an all-ductwork one); left as a disclosed, unfixed finding rather than patched quietly here.

runs.description: 1¼" hydronic branch, from the real drawn dead end at the HWS/HWR riser's isolation-valve gap to the elbow immediately ahead of coil unit HC-3/CV-3's own valve cluster. Supply vs. return identity of this specific line is not resolved -- see scope.
